findings: The selected candidate addresses the prior failure: it no longer attributes GN 1130 safety instructions to EH 22350 and explicitly treats support-before-extraction as the benchmark’s tested condition rather than a manufacturer-specific prohibition.

The manufacturer datasheet visually and textually supports the EH 22350.0621 identity, movable shackle, spring-button mounting/removal sequence, H11 receiving bore, shaft tolerance, dimensions, directional load ratings, and 277 g mass.
The selected row is read correctly: d1=10.0 mm with −0.04/−0.08 mm tolerance, l1=15 mm, F1/F2/F3=2.7/2.4/2.1 kN, x=1.5–10 mm, location hole=10.0 mm H11, and mass=277 g.

The build plan now specifies usable collision geometry: a 9.94 mm shaft and 10.06 mm bore give 0.12 mm diametral clearance. Unpublished button travel, ball geometry, cam behavior, shoulder, workpiece, and fixture values are clearly disclosed as representative testable assumptions.

The proposed rigid-body mechanism preserves the essential physical ability—button-controlled radial retention, load transfer through the movable shackle, fixture seating, unloading, and complete pin recovery—and calls for native joints, colliders, and diagnostic controls without object-state writes or fake grasp welds.
The evidence supports attempting construction; completed physics trials, robot demonstrations, and novelty certification correctly remain later gates.
